title: Cross-mailbox Gmail Move
blurb: Connected-mailbox Move accepts Gmail API sources only after verified Copy and a separate explicit source Trash review; no user or environment switch widens provider support. IMAP receiving mailboxes must independently pass Copy capability and preservation checks. IMAP, Outlook, Yahoo, legacy Gmail IMAP and Local Folders sources cannot use connected Move. Existing Local Folders transfers keep their separate behavior. Copy, then review Gmail Trash first completes ordinary verified Copy. Copy confirmation never authorizes source Trash. A separate Move review must match fresh existing Copy receipts, the exact source messages and receiving folder, followed by a second Move Gmail originals to Trash confirmation. Cancelling that review keeps both sources and destination copies. The source service never uploads or reuploads. Gmail Trash affects originals across all labels and provider retention can later delete them. Copy and Trash are not atomic; there is no Undo. Stop, changed choices, reconnect, source or destination identity changes, mailbox navigation, closing and window destruction retire the source review and fence later writes; an already started Gmail request cannot be recalled. Confirmed source Trash adopts Gmail label evidence transactionally, including cached label aliases. A failed local cache update leaves the confirmed provider receipt intact and shows refresh pending; it never retries Trash. Partial results retain verified destination copies. Unknown source outcomes stop remaining work, preserve both receipts and never automatically retry; check Gmail before further action. No bot, CLI command, automatic replay or release enablement is added. Synthetic DOM and Chromium checks do not certify live providers, native Windows/macOS, power loss or screen-reader behavior.
